column1: # Bulgakov on Викитека, drafted by tools/wikisource_author.py and gone over by hand.
# Columns: slug, Wikisource page, author, title, category, blurb.
# The @ marks the draft put on every page with a subpage have been taken off.
# Wikisource's EPUB export already follows a work's chapter subpages — that is
# how Белая гвардия came in with its nineteen chapters — and most of those
# subpages were a /ДО edition in the old orthography rather than chapters.
# @ is for the other kind: an index whose members are separate pages. Записки
# юного врача is the one here, and its seven stories are commented out below
# so the cycle arrives as one book rather than as seven fragments and a shell.
# Blurbs are written only where they can be written truthfully; the rest are
# left blank on purpose and are easier to write from the imported text.

column6: A clerk at the Match Supply Depot is sacked over a misread signature, and chases the official who signed it through a Moscow that will not hold still.
A zoologist finds a ray that makes living things grow at monstrous speed, and a state farm takes it away from him to save the country's chickens.
A doctor of twenty-three, a month out of university, is sent alone to a country hospital forty versts from the railway and learns his trade on whoever is carried through the door.
The notebooks of a young country doctor who began with a quarter-syringe against a pain in the stomach, left to the colleague who reads them after his death.
Cuffs written on in the Caucasus and in Moscow: a writer with typhus, no money and no papers, talking his way from one office to the next.
An unfinished letter to a friend about how he came to write, and the first form of what later became Театральный роман.
A count's house, now a museum, is shown to day trippers by the old servant who stayed with it, and one visitor in dark glasses knows the rooms too well.
Gogol's Chichikov wakes up in Soviet Moscow, registers himself as a citizen, and finds the new institutions even easier to rob than the old.
From a room he is not allowed to leave, a man writes to his mother about the brother he watched ride away and did not call back.
A grand Moscow apartment house, requisitioned and packed to the attics, burns down because no one is permitted to light a stove.
A Chinese man alone in Moscow with no language, no papers and no bread is taken in by a machine-gun detachment.
Two sentries on a railway line in the freezing dark, and the raid that comes for them.
At the end of an evening among doctors, one of them answers the question of whether he has ever killed a man.
How the author got through the winter of 1920 in Vladikavkaz by writing a revolutionary play in three days.
A night in Kiev as the city changes hands, taken from a novel he never finished.
A doctor's civil-war notebook in fragments: mobilised, sent south, and moved about the country by other people's armies.
A native's sketch of Kiev after the civil war — its hills and churches, its wrecked bridges, and a city that changed hands more times than anyone could count.
An article written from the White south in 1919: the war will be paid for, and the bill will fall on the people who did not start it.
